33.0.s.en: 1. Between the sober fearer of the Lord and the light-minded fool

33.0.0.en: 1 He who fears the Lord will meet no harm, but in temptation the Lord will keep him, and deliver him from evils. 2 The wise man does not hate the Law, but he who is a hypocrite in it is like a ship in a whirlwind. 3 The intelligent man believes the Law, and the Law is faithful to him. 4 Prepare your speech, as the righteous do in their questions, and you will be heard. Arrange the meanings of your knowledge and answer. 5 The inward parts of the fool are like the wheel of a cart, and his thought is like a lightly turning axle. 6 The mocking friend is like a stallion that neighs under every rider.

33.0.1.en: No evil befalls him who fears the Lord, but He (the Lord) delivers him in temptation again and again [1].

33.0.2.en: The fearer of God, the man of God, is in a unique position; he realizes that he is in the mind of God, as the beloved of the Lord, and is not in fear lest temptation or trials overtake him, for God delivers him and turns the trials into enjoyment, entering into eternal glories. This is our faith which moves us to prayer and stirs in us joyful hope. This was fulfilled the more through the Incarnation of the Word of God, for a great position has become ours; therefore the Apostle exulted, saying: "And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory" (1 Tim 3:16). By Him we enjoy righteousness and defy all the powers of darkness.

33.0.3.en: * Let us put on our heads the helmet of salvation, lest we be wounded and die in the battle.

33.0.4.en: Let us gird our loins with truth, that we may not be found weak in the fight.

33.0.5.en: Let us rise and awaken Christ, that He may calm the waves for us.

33.0.6.en: Let us take the shield against the evil one, as the preparation of the Gospel of our Savior (Eph 6:15-16).

33.0.7.en: Let us receive from our Lord the authority to tread on serpents and scorpions (Lk 10:19)...

33.0.8.en: Let us rejoice in our hope at all times (Rom 12:12), that he who is our hope and our Savior may rejoice in us...

33.0.9.en: Let us take for ourselves a weapon for the battle (Eph 6:16), which is the preparation for the Gospel.

33.0.10.en: Let us knock at the door of heaven (Mt 7:7), and it will be opened before us and we will enter in.

33.0.11.en: Let us ask for mercy with diligence, and we shall receive what is necessary for us...

33.0.12.en: Let us lift up our eyes on high, to see the radiance that is revealed.

33.0.13.en: Let us lift up our wings like the eagles, to see where the carcase is (Mt 24:28)...

33.0.14.en: He who has two wings flies with them away from him (from Satan), so that the arrows which he shoots toward him do not reach him?

33.0.15.en: The spiritual see him fighting, and his weapon has no power over their bodies.

33.1.0.en: All the children of light do not fear him, for darkness flees before the light. The children of the Good One do not fear the evil one, for He has given them to tread upon him with their feet (Gen 3:15) [2].

33.1.1.en: St. Aphrahat the Sage He does not hate the Law, but he who claims to keep it is like a boat in the storm [2].

33.1.2.en: While the believer lives kept in the hands of God and does not fear temptations, the man who is a hypocrite in keeping the divine commandment is never free from anxiety, like a small boat in the midst of a violent storm. It turns a man's life from a pleasant journey in the company of the Lord, going forward quietly toward heaven, into a boat in the midst of a dangerous tempest.

33.2.0.en: The man of understanding trusts in the Law, and the Law is trustworthy to him, because it is a divine revelation [3].

33.2.1.en: The wise man of God believes in God through His word, and so understands God's plan for him, trusts in His divine promises, and counts himself blessed, because God reveals to him His divine mysteries.

33.3.0.en: Prepare what you say, and you will be heard; gather your knowledge and answer [4].

33.3.1.en: How does the fearer of the Lord prepare himself to enter into an open dialogue with God, except by gathering all his inner powers? For he is enjoying the greatest moments of his life, as he stands before his Beloved.

33.3.2.en: * God does not need resounding speeches, nor eloquent words, for He knows what is useful to us. Thus we can define prayer as a work that is accomplished in a man's conscience and within him, and it is a work that extends to all the works that weave a man's life [3].

33.4.0.en: St. Basil the Great The heart of the fool is like the wheel of a cart, and his thoughts are like the revolving axle [5].

33.4.1.en: The fool lives in the whirlpool of life; he does not feel his way along the true road, nor does he know where he is going, and he turns around himself all his life. His mind is like a small light cart, with no wise driver to direct it; it does not perceive the straight road that leads to heaven, but remains in confusion and disorder.

33.4.2.en: The mocking friend is like a spirited horse, which neighs under everyone who rides it [4] [6].

33.4.3.en: The friend who mocks his friend is like a stallion that neighs under everyone who rides it; he gives out disturbing sounds with no meaning and no purpose.

33.4.4.en: * When the first man fell and disobeyed God, man became, as the Scripture says, like sheep [for Hades (Ps 49:14)], because he sinned against reason. For a good reason man was counted irrational like the animals. In a similar way Wisdom says: "The pleasure-seeker and the adulterer are like a stallion" (cf. Sir 33:6), because he has become like the animals, without reason. Therefore he added: "which neighs under every rider upon him." Such a man no longer speaks, for he who sins against reason is not rational, but a dumb beast surrendered to desire, upon whom any kind of pleasure can mount and lead him [5].

33.5.s.en: 2. The wise man and the need for God's grace

33.5.0.en: 7 Why is one day preferred to another, when the light of every day in the year comes from the sun? 8 The knowledge of the Lord distinguished them, when the sun was made which keeps the order, 9 and He varied the seasons; so the feasts were celebrated at the appointed hour. 10 Some of them He exalted and sanctified, and some He made among the number of ordinary days. And so all men are of the dust, and Adam was made of the earth, 11 but the Lord distinguished them in the fullness of His knowledge, and varied their ways. 12 Some of them He blessed and exalted, and some He sanctified and brought near to Himself, and some He cursed and brought low and cast down from their station. 13 As the clay is in the hand of the potter, and all its ways go according to his pleasure, 14 so men are in the hand of their Maker, and He recompenses them according to His judgment.

33.5.1.en: Why is one day better than another, when all the light of the days of the year comes from the sun? [7]

33.5.2.en: Although the source of illumination of all the days of the year is the very same sun, God has appointed holy days, seasons and feasts, and these days are distinguished from others. So out of the love of the Lord, the Sun of Righteousness, who lights all the days of our life with His divine righteousness, He gives us special days such as Sundays and the monthly and yearly feasts, which present to us declarations of the saving work of God, with a taste of the earnest of the heaven that He prepares for us.

33.6.0.en: It was the knowledge of the Lord that distinguished them, for He varied the seasons and the feasts [8].

33.6.1.en: God arranged this variety so that we might experience His plan in creation and salvation, and so desire to attain eternal life. And the Church calls us, through the church calendar, from the beginning of each church year to its end, not to cease from enjoying the experience of fellowship with the Holy Trinity, who loves all mankind! With every morning the believer sings with the prophet Jeremiah, whose heart's walls pained him (Jer 4:19) on account of the bereavement of the daughter of his people, whom their disobedience and estrangement from God was shattering; but through his inner experience and his assurance of the work of God, his depths are turned into a second heaven, and he says: "His compassions fail not. They are new every morning... The Lord is my portion, saith my soul" (Lam 3:23-24).

33.6.2.en: The secret of the exultation of the heart of St. Jacob of Serugh in the midst of his pains was his realization that the mountain of Golgotha is the "wedding of Golgotha"; he is crucified with the heavenly Bridegroom to rise each day with Him, and experiences the embrace of the Lord, the fountain of inner peace and heavenly joy! This is the role of the church calendar.

33.6.3.en: * It must be realized that it befits each one of us to prove whether he is in the days of good or in the days of evil. And does he possess "the days of Joshua," which are the days of righteousness, or does he possess the days of evil? For if we recognize "the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world" (Jn 1:9), and give ourselves up to Him to be enlightened, and if the "Sun of righteousness" (Mal 4:2) rises in us and lights the world of our souls, we shall possess "the days of Joshua," that is, the days of Jesus Christ, the days of salvation. But if someone gives himself up to "the light that shall be put out" (cf. Job 18:5), the light that is opposed to the truth, he will also possess days, but they are days of evil. He will not be in the days of Joshua, but in the days of Manasseh or Pharaoh, in the evil days of other kings.

33.7.0.en: Origen Some days He exalted and sanctified, and some days He made ordinary [9].

33.7.1.en: The Church calls us to make all our days the Lord's, so that we may enjoy continual joy, and she has established occasions that renew in us the remembrance of God's saving works and turn our life into a joyful, continual feast. We mention, by way of example, the following:

33.7.2.en: First: daily joy: in the prayer of Prime we enjoy the gladness of the Resurrection, and in the prayer of Midnight the gladness of the coming of the Bridegroom.

33.7.3.en: Second: weekly joy: on Sunday we enjoy the gladness of the Resurrection of Christ.

33.7.4.en: Third: monthly joy: where we enjoy the commemoration of the Annunciation, the Nativity and the Resurrection.

33.7.5.en: Fourth: yearly joyful commemorations and feasts.

33.8.0.en: And all men are of the dust, and from the earth Adam was created [10].

33.8.1.en: God deals through human history, distinguishing each man from his brother according to his seriousness in life and salvation, and his faithfulness in employing his powers and using his gifts. Therefore there are vast differences in the lives of men and their aspirations for life, although all are of the offspring of one man created of dust, namely Adam [10].

33.9.0.en: The Lord distinguished them in the fullness of His wisdom, and changed their ways [11].

33.9.1.en: God in His love for men gave each man his various gifts and abilities so that all might live together, each one completing the other. This variety lends humanity beauty, love and humility; each person needs his brother.

33.10.0.en: Some of the days He blessed and exalted, and some of the days He sanctified and brought near to Himself, and some of the days He cursed and abased and removed from their station [12].

33.10.1.en: It is clear that by his talk of days here he means the days of man. He made plain that all men are equal since they were created of dust, and God gave them various talents, so He blesses and sanctifies some days, and permits humiliation in some days. By this he calls us to serious thought about our life and our mission.

33.10.2.en: a. God wishes to bless all days; on His part He spreads out His hands to give us His blessing, but if we give Him the back and not the face (Jer 2:27), even the days of feasts become hateful to Him (Isa 1:13).

33.10.3.en: b. The assurance that man's life is open to change, so that it befits the believer, if he falls, to return to God in a spirit of hope.

33.10.4.en: c. To realize that God's wisdom is above human thinking, for God may permit a man to be humbled for no apparent reason, but only that the Lord may carry him over into glory for his own edification and the edification of many, as happened with the righteous young man Joseph the son of Jacob.

33.10.5.en: d. It befits the rich, the people of authority and the church leaders to adorn themselves with humility, and what they enjoy is a divine gift. When the children of Israel, as the people of God, grew haughty, He permitted them the humiliation of the Babylonian captivity for seventy years.

33.10.6.en: All His ways are according to His good pleasure, like the clay in the hand of the potter.

33.11.0.en: So men are in the hand of their Maker, and He recompenses them according to His judgment [13].

33.11.1.en: The Holy Scripture calls us to submit to the will of our Creator, that we may experience His work in us as the Lover of mankind (cf. Isa 45:9; 64:7; Jer 18:6). And the Apostle says: "Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?" (Rom 9:21). God gives us the Spirit of adoption, that we may know His divine mysteries, and so long to enjoy the eternal glory that He prepares for us. And on our part it befits us to realize that we are "a potsherd of the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or shall it say, Thy work has no hands? Woe unto him that saith unto his father, What begettest thou? or to the woman, What hast thou brought forth?" (Isa 45:9-10). St. John Chrysostom [6] affirms that the Apostle wishes to present one aspect of the parable, namely that God works in us and we can do nothing but obey. But He does not take away from us the freedom of our will; if we wish to live with Him, He changes us for the glory of His name, in a manner that surpasses our understanding.

33.12.0.en: 15 Over against evil is good, and over against death is life; so over against the godly is the sinner. And so consider all the works of the Most High; you will find them two by two, one over against the other.

33.12.1.en: Good is the opposite of evil, and life is the opposite of death, and in the same way the sinner is the opposite of the godly [14].

33.12.2.en: So consider all the works of the Most High; they appear two by two, the one over against the other [15].

33.12.3.en: A man's life is either good or evil, he is a sinner or a righteous man; there is no position between the two, "for whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath" (Mt 13:12). On the other hand, the good God is able to turn evil into good. The Cross of the Lord of glory Jesus is a unique example of bringing forth good out of evil. He presents the grace of salvation through the Cross which the enemy of good prepared for destruction.

33.12.4.en: St. Augustine sees in this statement a revelation of the purpose of the book, which is to offer good instead of evil, and life instead of death, so that man may look to the works of the Most High, who works in the sinner that he may become godly [7].

33.13.s.en: 4. The scribe, the teacher, gleans behind the grape gatherers

33.13.0.en: 16 I, the last, have awakened, and have inherited these things as they were from the beginning. 17 Like one who gleans behind the grape gatherers, I came with the blessing of the Lord; and I filled the winepress like one who had gathered. 18 See how my labor was not for myself alone, but also for all who seek instruction. 19 Hear me, O great men of the people, and give ear to me, O rulers of the congregation.

33.13.1.en: I was the last to awaken to glean in the vineyard behind the grape gatherers [16].

33.13.2.en: In a spirit of humility Ben Sirach presents an example for us to follow; with his surpassing gifts and the wonderful work of God in his life, he did not boast of his wisdom. Rather he reckoned himself as one who gleans behind the grape gatherers. He reckoned himself like Ruth the Gentile maiden, who gathered the ears of grain behind the reapers with care and striving, without slackness, and so became a grandmother of Jesus Christ, the divine ear of grain who gives life, satisfaction and glory to His believers of all peoples, nations and tongues. This is what gladdened the heart of Ben Sirach, that his striving and watching were not enjoyed by him alone, but he offered them to all who seek instruction.

33.14.0.en: By the blessing of the Lord I arrived at the right time, and filled my winepress like one who gathered grapes [17].

33.14.1.en: Ben Sirach, as a teacher, observed that some present questions on trivial matters far from the salvation of the soul; so while not despising his students, the teacher tries to direct his students toward what is for edification.

33.14.2.en: The Lord Christ, who works in good teachers, in His dialogue with the Samaritan woman, who tried to steer the conversation away from the salvation of her soul, spoke to her gently without wounding her feelings as a woman living with a man who was not her husband, and led her to the divine truth. He looked upon the woman as an ear of grain fallen from the reapers which it befitted Him to gather, as Ruth used to do, but He raised her to a better level for her salvation. This is what Naomi did with Ruth, for she accepted her striving in gathering the fallen ears of grain, yet directed her toward the owner of the field, Boaz, and so she became the grandmother of the unique divine ear of grain, Jesus the son of David, the Bread that came down from heaven, the giver of salvation and satisfaction.

33.14.3.en: In brief, while not despising the gleaning of what falls from the reapers, we must raise those whom we shepherd and serve to a surpassing heavenly level. One of the brothers asked Father the Elder Barsanuphius about a cowl that a brother had sent to him, whether he should accept it or not. The answer of the Elder came to him that this matter should not occupy him, lest he spoil his time in trivial things, but that he must care for the plentiful harvest that is on behalf of the Kingdom of God.

33.14.4.en: * Brother, I have sent you wisdom: "Be free, what do you want? Turn to yourself: 'The harvest truly is plenteous' (Mt 3:16). Leave everything, and give your time to the harvest and gathering, that you may have fruits of wheat and wine (Ps 4:7; Deut 33:28), that your heart may be strengthened and become joyful in the Lord. As for the cowl, if the brother wishes to give it to you with all his heart, accept it, and condemn yourself as unworthy [8].

33.15.0.en: St. Barsanuphius Observe well that my labor was not for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction [18].

33.15.1.en: He compared himself with the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the prophets, and realized that he was like one who gathers ears of grain behind the reapers. And in a spirit of hope he realized that his labor would not be lost in vain, but by the grace of God all who seek instruction would benefit from it.

33.16.0.en: Hear me, O leaders of the people, and give ear to me, O rulers of the congregation [19].

33.16.1.en: Ben Sirach realized by the Spirit of God that all who seek instruction benefit from his work, so he dared to speak with the leaders of the people and the rulers of the congregation. True humility moves a man to work in a spirit of strength, even among leaders and rulers!

33.17.s.en: 5. Do not be under anyone's guardianship!

33.17.0.en: 20 Do not put in authority over yourself in your lifetime your son or your wife or your brother or your friend, and do not give your goods to another, lest you regret it and have to beg him for them. 21 As long as you live and breath is in you, do not give yourself over to any man, 22 for it is better that your sons should ask of you than that you should look to the hands of your sons. 23 In all your affairs keep your preeminence, 24 and do not leave a blemish on your honor. Divide your inheritance at the end of the days of your life, when death is at hand. 25 Fodder and the rod and burdens are for the ass, and bread and discipline and work for the servant. 26 Set the slave to work and you will have rest; slacken his hands and he will seek liberty.

33.17.1.en: Do not put in authority over yourself in your lifetime your son or your wife or your brother or your friend, and do not give your possessions to another, lest you change your mind and have to beg for them [20].

33.18.0.en: As long as you live and breath is in you, do not let anyone take your place [21].

33.19.0.en: It is better that your sons should ask of you than that you should look to the hands of your sons [22].

33.19.1.en: The believer longs to see every man a leader who takes pride in the work of God in him and with him; the wise father gives his sons and his wife the opportunity to share with him in the management of the family's affairs and his administration of all the aspects of the family, for their good as for his own; in a spirit of wisdom he does not hand everything over to them during his lifetime:

33.19.2.en: a. Sons are sometimes exposed to deviation, as happened with the prodigal son (Lk 15), who squandered all that he received.

33.19.3.en: b. A person himself may be exposed to a crisis because of illness or the country's economic circumstances, and when he asks his children they may not respond to him. So it is wise to give them a share during his lifetime, and to write a will concerning the rest of his possessions, keeping it with him and informing them of where it is.

33.20.0.en: Be distinguished in all your works, and do not disfigure your reputation [23].

33.20.1.en: Although a father loves his children more than he cares for himself, Ben Sirach wishes the father to keep the authority of love, so that the image of the loving, wise father and manager remains until the moments of his death.

33.21.0.en: On the day when you complete the days of your life, and at the time of your death, divide your inheritance [24].

33.21.1.en: The father does not leave his children to enter into disputes about the distribution of his wealth, but arranges the matter of the inheritance among them with justice, wisdom and frankness before his death if possible.

33.22.s.en: 6. Let each man do what suits his role and gifts

33.22.0.en: 27 The yoke and the thongs bow the neck, and constant work subdues the slave. 28 For the wicked slave there are torments and torture. Compel him to work lest he be idle, 29 for idleness teaches many kinds of wickedness. 30 Put him to the works that befit him; and if he does not obey, make his fetters heavy, but do not be excessive in the punishment of any person of flesh, and do nothing without discernment. 31 If you have a slave, let him be to you as yourself, for you acquired him with blood. If you have a slave, treat him as yourself, for you need him as you need yourself. 32 If you hurt him, he will run away, 33 and if he flees and goes away, in what way will you seek him?

33.22.1.en: Fodder and the rod and burdens are for the ass, and bread and discipline and work for the servant [25].

33.22.2.en: While looking upon the slave (or servant) as a brother, the master must care for three things:

33.22.3.en: a. Providing fodder or bread, so that he does not leave him hungry or deprived of food.

33.22.4.en: b. The rod, which is understood as the exercise of firmness together with love, so that he realizes his limits without injustice on the master's part.

33.22.5.en: c. Work in moderation; for to burden him beyond his strength is counted as violence which may drive him to rebellion, and indulgence toward him may drive him to laziness, and this is not for his good spiritually, physically or socially.

33.22.6.en: Put your slave to work and you will find rest; release his hands and he will seek freedom [26].

33.22.7.en: If the laws at that time ignored the right of slaves as human beings, the Law did not leave the master to control them in an absolute manner. Directing the slave to work that suits his strength gives the master a kind of rest.

33.22.8.en: The yoke and the thongs bow the neck, and for the wicked slave there are torments and pain [27].

33.22.9.en: As Sirach defends the rights of slaves, so he asks for the wise discipline of the rebellious and those who spoil the work, for the good of both parties.

33.23.0.en: Compel him to work lest he be idle, for idleness teaches many evils [28].

33.23.1.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that the expression "idleness" has a wider meaning than mere "not working," for he sees that one who works merely to acquire vain food is counted idle, and he sees that one who exhausts all his strength and energy merely to eat is working for the sake of vain food. St. John Chrysostom calls us to work in order to offer to the Lord Christ food and drink and clothing, for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven; this food is not vain, but truly remains forever [9].

33.23.2.en: * The prohibition of excessive care for the needs of our body does not forbid care and work altogether. It remains for us to work for ourselves, not for the perishing food, but for the food that endures for eternal life (Jn 6:27), not only for our bodily needs, but also to relieve our neighbor (Eph 4:28). And the Lord will say to us on the day of judgment: "I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink..." (Mt 25:35). What we do for those who have consecrated themselves to Him is counted as though we did it with them, and for it the heavenly Kingdom is given to us. And those who did not work and did not toil to help the weak and serve their neighbor will be punished, and He will send them to eternal torment (Mt 25:41-46) [10].

33.24.0.en: St. Basil the Great Put him to work as befits him, and if he does not obey, make his feet heavy with fetters [29].

33.24.1.en: Idleness is harmful to the master as to the slave, to the child as to the old man, even to the sick. It befits all mankind to work according to their gifts, time and abilities. Sts. Pachomius and Basil often affirmed the monk's obligation to work for their spiritual edification.

33.25.0.en: And do not behave arrogantly toward any flesh, and do nothing without judgment [30].

33.25.1.en: Ben Sirach was careful that the students should not fall into the letter that kills, so he requires them to practice everything with prudence and not by the literal execution of the commandment.

33.26.0.en: If you have a slave, let him be as yourself, for you acquired him with your blood [31].

33.26.1.en: Sirach prepares the Jews and the Gentiles for the acceptance of the Lord Christ the Savior, who spreads out His hands to embrace, if possible, all mankind without partiality for race, age, position or abilities. For all were created of dust, and for all the Savior offers Himself as a sacrifice on their behalf, and behold, He prepares places in heaven for everyone who believes in Him and responds to Him.

33.27.0.en: If you have a slave, treat him as a brother, for you need him as you need yourself [32].

33.27.1.en: Without doubt this statement represents a revolt against the system of slavery, not by violence but by sound thinking.

33.28.0.en: If you wrong him, and he flees away, in what way will you go to seek him? [33]

33.28.1.en: He warns against mistreating slaves. He lived in an age when man enslaved his brother in humanity, and there was no law to protect slaves. He is preparing the way for the liberation of slaves! He required the master to reckon his slaves as himself, to treat them as brothers, highlighting their mutual need. This opinion provoked the Roman rulers, because the empire at that time had sixty million slaves, and it was feared that this teaching might drive them to revolt against their masters, which portended a revolution of unwelcome consequences, and perhaps this was one of the causes of the persecution of Christianity. "Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven" (Col 4:1).

33.28.2.en: * Let social differences be wiped out, so that there is no subjection and authority, poverty and extravagant wealth, nobles and commoners, a degraded family and an honored family, and no room for inequality... Let us judge by political and legislative equality, and let it be distributed to each one in complete freedom, and in a manner full of peace, that he may choose what he wishes [11].

33.28.3.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa Inspired by Sirach 33

33.29.s.en: Grant me wisdom and good management

33.29.0.en: * Nail Your fear within me, that I may not fear temptations.

33.29.1.en: I hold fast to Your true promises, and my soul is at peace.

33.29.2.en: Take away from me all folly, that I may not walk in a vicious circle!

33.29.3.en: * Let me cling to You, and You will sanctify all my days for You.

33.29.4.en: You shine with Your light, O Sun of Righteousness, upon my life, and my life is turned into a perpetual feast and glorious joy.

33.29.5.en: * I am dust and ashes, but Your gifts to me are surpassing.

33.29.6.en: With every morning my soul sets out from glory to glory.

33.29.7.en: The touches of Your hand raise me up as a vessel of honor, O greatest Potter.

33.29.8.en: I confess to You my weaknesses, and You turn my evil into true good, and raise me from darkness to light, and from death to eternal life!

33.29.9.en: * Count me like Ruth the Gentile, gleaning behind the reapers.

33.29.10.en: I possess You, O divine ear of grain, and You make me of the household of God.

33.29.11.en: You promised me that You do not forget a cup of cold water, so accept my service to everyone who seeks true instruction.

33.29.12.en: * Give me the spirit of wisdom with love, that I may know how to give generously and with good management!

33.29.13.en: Grant me not to cease from the good fight.

33.29.14.en: That I may not fall into despair, nor haughtiness come upon me!

33.29.15.en: Teach me not to despise any man, for You came down to take the last rank of mankind.

33.29.16.en: You spread out Your hands on the Cross, and embrace sinners and fornicators and sanctify them.

33.29.17.en: Let every man be as myself, that I may ignore no one.

33.29.18.en: For I wish that all may become members in Your body, O Holy One!
